chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who divorces his wife, does he provide her with mut'ah (provision)? He said: Yes. Does he not love to be among the do-gooders? Does he not want to be among the pious?

key_terms.الْمُحْسِنِينَ: The do-gooders / those who excel in good deeds
key_terms.يُمَتِّعُهَا: He provides her with mut'ah (parting gift)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on providing for a divorced wife in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the obligation of mut'ah for a revocably divorced wife, grounding the legal requirement in the spiritual aspiration of the husband. By asking 'Does he not love to be among the do-gooders?', the Imam elevates the financial duty from a mere contractual obligation to an act of worship that reflects taqwa (God-consciousness). This highlights the Shia emphasis on the moral character of the provider as integral to the validity of the divorce proceedings.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who divorces his wife, shall he provide for her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Does he not love to become one of the do-gooders? Does he not want to become one of the pious?’
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn af-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the case of a man who divorces his wife; if he can benefit her. He (the Imam) said, ’Yes, does he not want to be of the people of good deeds, does he not want to be of the pious people?”’
